title: Pilot-to-Scale runbook: KPI ownership & readiness grid
content:
SUMMARY:
This is a compact runbook for moving features from pilot -> scale. Focus: (1) a lightweight KPI ownership grid to remove ambiguity, (2) a short readiness checklist per launch lane (beta/pilot/staged-scale), (3) a procedural handoff for infra/product/CS when committing to scale. Designed to be used in weekly product-ops sync and as a living artifact during the 6-week ramp window.

GOAL:
Minimize friction and rework when a pilot hits scale criteria. Move decisions from ad-hoc to signal-driven with clear owners and timeboxed actions.

KEY DEFINITIONS (as used below):
- Pilot: feature gated to small cohort (<5% of customers) to validate ops signals and core correctness.
- Scale: opening feature to broad population with SLO/throughput expectations.
- Ramp window: monitored period after enabling broader traffic (typ 2–6 weeks).

PHASES & PRIMARY DECISIONS:
1) Pilot validation (owner: PM) — decide to escalate to scaled rollout if KPIs stable for 7 consecutive days.
2) Pre-scale hardening (owner: Eng lead + Infra TPM) — address capacity, fallback, ops runbooks.
3) Scale rollout (owner: Product Ops) — coordinate staged traffic increase and final signoffs.

KPI OWNERSHIP GRID (compact)
- Column headers (represented as lines): KPI / Target / Measurement cadence / Primary owner / Backup owner / Gate threshold
- KPIs: availability (p95 success rate), median tail latency, cost per 1k requests (billing), quality (user-sentiment NPS proxy or eval pass rate), error rate by class (auth, infra, model), ops incident rate (pageable events/week)

Example rows (text format):
- availability | >= 99.9% p95 success | daily | Eng-SRE (Diego Ramos) | Eng lead (Arjun Patel) | < 99.9% -> block 
- tail latency | tail p99 < 800ms | daily | Serving runtime (Arjun Patel) | Infra TPM (Iris Nguyen) | p99 > 1s -> rollback canary
- cost | <= $0.95/1k tokens (or per request threshold) | weekly | Finance ops (Leah Kim) | PM (Maya Thompson) | > 20% increase MoM -> review
- quality | sample eval pass rate >= 94% / manual review pass 90% | daily sampling | Research (Iris Nguyen) | PM (Maya Thompson) | drop > 4pp -> pause cadence
- ops pages | <= 1 page/week during ramp | weekly | SRE (Diego Ramos) | On-call lead | >1/week -> investigate root cause before next increase

READINESS CHECKLIST (pre-scale) - short actionable items, tick when done:
- [ ] Canary pattern validated for 48h under target traffic (note: run 3x synthetic scenarios)
- [ ] Fallback variant validated (compatible model variant / cheaper endpoint)
- [ ] Capacity plan signed (GPU pool, autoscale thresholds, burst policies) by Infra TPM
- [ ] Cost guardrails configured (alerts for >15% delta within 24h)
- [ ] Observability dashboards created + owner assigned (per-route breakdown, token cost)
- [ ] Runbook shortlink exists and is surfaced on on-call rotation
- [ ] Security review (data handling, PII masks) completed for pilot data set
- [ ] Customer success playbook drafted for first 10 escalations

SCALE RAMP PLAY (day-by-day condensed):
- DAY 0 (GO): enable staged ramp at 10% traffic; product-ops posts kickoff note; monitoring alerts watched 
- DAY 1–2: monitor KPIs hourly; SRE on high alert; rollback criteria documented
- DAY 3–7: if all signals green, increment to 30% then 60% over next 3 days; do a midpoint review on DAY7
- WEEK 2: full 100% if SLOs stable for 7 days; continue ramp window monitoring for 4 additional weeks

ESCALATION & DECISION RULES (explicit):
- Immediate rollback: any data-loss or PII exposure incident; otherwise, p95 availability drop below 99% for 1h triggers rollback to previous stable variant.
- Pause & triage: quality drop > 4 percentage points or cost increase > 30% vs baseline triggers a pause and 24h triage.
- Executive alert: sustained incident (>=3 pages within 72h) -> notify GTM lead + Head of Product Ops.

HANDOFF CHECKLIST (who signs the final go):
- PM: product acceptance (feature behaves as spec) — signature: Maya Thompson
- Eng lead: capacity and fallback verified — signature: Arjun Patel
- SRE: runbooks and alerting in place — signature: Diego Ramos
- Finance: cost guardrails enabled — signature: Leah Kim
- CS/Support: support playbook & escalation channels documented — signature: TBD
- Legal/Sec: compliance OK for scale (if required) — signature: Iris Nguyen

RISK LOG (short bullets - to keep light):
- Model drift risk: need daily eval sampling during ramp; instrument synthetic prompts.
- Unexpected cost with long-tail inputs: add token limits & guardrails during pilot.
- Customer confusion: ensure feature flagging and rollout notes to top 50 customers.

OPEN QUESTIONS (things we should decide before committing to scale):
- What is the acceptable transient cost bump during a 2-week ramp? (Finance to propose threshold)
- Which SLOs get priority if there is a conflict (latency vs cost vs quality)?
- Who owns customer communication for high-impact rollbacks?

QUICK REFERENCES (links & tickets):
- Pilot instrumentation confluence: confluence:PRODOPS-2145
- Pre-scale infra checklist PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/214
- Tracking epic: JIRA:POPS-982

NOTES TO SELF / USAGE: (informal)
- Use this doc in Monday product-ops sync; update the ownership grid as owners rotate.
- Keep examples specific to the feature — rewrite KPI targets per feature baseline.
- If we’re scaling a security-sensitive pilot, insert Legal as a hard stop for go.

REVISION HISTORY (brief):
- 2025-09-18: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-11-02: added cost guardrail language (Leah)
- 2026-02-20: tightened rollback thresholds and annotated owners (Arjun)

END.
